segments.text: This is Max and Mia podcast.

segments.text: We really appreciate all of you listeners out there. Absolutely.

segments.text: Whether you're listening during your morning coffee, on your way to work, or just relaxing at home,
segments.ipa: /ˈwɛðər jʊr ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈdʊrɪŋ jɔr ˈmɔrnɪŋ ˈkɑfi ɑn jɔr weɪ tu wɝk ɔr dʒʌst rɪˈlæksɪŋ æt hoʊm/

segments.text: Today, we have something a bit different and exciting for you.

segments.text: We know that sometimes English can be tricky, especially when words sound very similar,
segments.ipa: /wi noʊ ðæt səmˈtaɪmz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ kæn bi ˈtrɪki əˈspɛʃli wɛn wɝdz saʊnd ˈvɛri ˈsɪmələr/

segments.text: You know those moments when you hear someone speaking and you think, "Wait, did they say look or luck?"

segments.text: Or maybe, "Were they talking about where or were?" Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ˈmeɪbi wɝ ðeɪ ˈtɔkɪŋ əˈbaʊt wɛr ɔr wɝ ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: So, today we're focusing on training your ears.

segments.text: We've prepared two natural conversations for you.

segments.text: And here's the challenge.
segments.ipa: /ənd hɪrz ðə ˈtʃæləndʒ/

segments.text: Try not to rely too much on the subtitles this time.

segments.text: Don't worry though.
segments.ipa: /doʊnt ˈwɝi ðoʊ/

segments.text: Even if some words sound the same to you, the context will help you understand which word we're actually using.
segments.ipa: /ˈivɪn ɪf sʌm wɝdz saʊnd ðə seɪm tu ju ðə ˈkɑntɛkst wɪl hɛlp ju ˌʌndərˈstænd wɪtʃ wɝd wir ˈækˌtʃuəli ˈjuzɪŋ/

segments.text: That's a super important skill in real English conversations.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈsupər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt skɪl ɪn ril ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz/

segments.text: Are you ready to challenge your listening skills?

segments.ipa: /aɪm stɪl ˈtraɪɪŋ tu ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪt ɔl/

segments.ipa: /aɪ min aɪv bɪn ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ðɪs ˌɑpərˈtunəti fɔr mʌnθs noʊ weɪ/

segments.text: That's such a relief, right? Exactly.

segments.text: An actual pool.

segments.text: Now I'm seriously jealous.
